public_rationale: The ILO found limits to whole-job automation, and earlier Danish surveys found modest time savings. Those findings fit part of Zitron's point. Anthropic's usage analysis also shows substantial task-directed activity, although it cannot measure verified automation across workers' actual workloads. These sources measure different things and do not settle how much ordinary work could reliably be automated in the target period.
limitations: The target month is an explicit interpretation of an undated ongoing claim.
The Danish evidence predates the target period.
Anthropic's classifications do not establish successful autonomous completion.
Potential occupational exposure is not actual automation.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI can do very little to actually automate people's real jobs.

statement.excerpt: Companies can raise their prices specifically to raise their profits, Meta can literally not make a metaverse, AI can do very little to actually automate your real job, and the media will still tell you to shut the fuck up and eat their truth-slop.

our_interpretation: In this post, AI means generative AI and LLM-based systems.

The plain reading is that these systems could reliably take over only a small part of ordinary workers' actual workloads. It does not require complete replacement of a worker before automation counts.
Capability, deployment, time saved, and whole-job replacement are distinct measures.
No period is supplied. I use May 2025, the most recent completed month before publication, for the ongoing capability claim. Earlier measurements are context.
Very little is read as a small practical share, without inventing a numerical cutoff.
criteria.support_condition: Representative workplace evidence shows that reliable automation covered only a small share of ordinary workloads in the target period, including the human work needed to check and correct outputs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence shows substantial reliable automation across ordinary workloads in the target period. A narrow successful deployment alone does not settle the general claim.

evidence.explanation: The Danish surveys found modest reported time savings among chatbot users. These earlier observations concern realized benefits, not the full capability of systems available in May 2025.

The conversation analysis indicates meaningful task-directed automation, challenging an expansive dismissal of usefulness. The denominator is sampled interactions, not all working time; the source cannot verify workplace use, downstream correction, or representative adoption.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative evidence for the target period measuring the share of work reliably completed by generative AI, including correction and supervision, would test the ordinary small-versus-substantial reading.
